assessment.nobel_worthiness: Very high. Random-coefficients demand estimation with endogenous prices and the dynamic oligopoly framework turned industrial organisation into a quantitative empirical field. The tools are used routinely in merger review, antitrust, trade, health and environmental economics, so the impact reaches well beyond IO.
assessment.attribution: The Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes demand framework is cleanly attributable to the three proposed names. Pakes also anchors the dynamic-game and estimation side (Ericson-Pakes, Olley-Pakes). Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are significant, but a three-person limit leaves them out. Bresnahan is the main alternative and possible fourth-name risk.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The core papers date from the 1990s and have decades of confirmed use, replication and extension. There is no timing concern.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee prefers to credit Bresnahan's earlier new-empirical-IO work over or alongside Levinsohn.
Whether the prize is seen as methodological, with the applied findings credited elsewhere.
Recent prizes have favoured identification and causal methods, which could compete for attention.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Very high. Staggered contracts and nominal price setting, the Taylor rule, and the micro-founded New Keynesian synthesis are the working framework of modern central banking and monetary-policy analysis. The policy and academic impact is enormous.
assessment.attribution: The credit is spread across a large group (Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gali, Gertler, Smets and others). The proposed trio is the plausible conceptual core: Calvo's pricing, Taylor's contracts and rule, and Woodford's unification. Any three-person selection will be contested.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature. The key ideas date from the 1980s to the early 2000s and have been tested through several policy regimes. Their performance in the post-2020 inflation episode adds new evidence but has not undermined the framework.
uncertainties: Attribution is genuinely diffuse and an optimal trio is debatable.
Recent inflation dynamics and heterogeneous-agent critiques could affect how the framework's legacy is judged.
Overlap with prior macro prizes (Lucas, Prescott-Kydland, Sargent-Sims) may matter.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High. Formal and empirical analysis of how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity shape fiscal policy and development created modern political economics. The field has influenced work on institutions, growth and public finance, and it complements the institutions prize of 2024.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini (the book and the constitutional-rules papers) are the clear centre. Besley adds state capacity, accountability and the development side. The three names are a coherent group, though others in the field could be argued for.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The central contributions date from the 1990s and 2000s, with extensive follow-up empirical work confirming and refining the main claims.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee sees this as too close to the recently honoured institutions work.
Some constitutional-effects findings rest on cross-country identification that is debated.
One of Besley's other lines of work might be preferred over the state-capacity strand.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High. The law-and-finance programme showed systematically that investor protection and legal institutions are associated with financial development, ownership structure and growth. It opened a very large empirical literature across finance, law and development.
assessment.attribution: The core papers are jointly authored by the proposed three, with Vishny as co-author of the earlier corporate-governance work. The listed credit is clear but a three-person cap excludes Vishny, which may be contentious.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with 25+ years of follow-up. That time has also produced serious criticism of the legal-origins thesis (measurement, endogeneity, historical interpretation), and the evidence is mixed.
uncertainties: The causal interpretation of legal origins remains contested.
Shleifer's broader body of work spans several fields. Whether credit here is framed narrowly or broadly is unclear.
Vishny's omission from a three-name proposal is a potential attribution weakness.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High. Foundations of open-economy macroeconomics: intertemporal approach to the current account, exchange-rate dynamics and the disconnect puzzles. The textbook and papers shaped how international macro is taught and conducted, and informed policy debate on exchange-rate regimes and capital flows.
assessment.attribution: Clear and compact: the joint 1996 text and the individual and joint papers support a two-person award. Redo or Obstfeld-Rogoff's Redux framework with Rogoff's separate contributions makes the credit well defined. Rogoff also appears in B003, so any award for Rogoff would draw on a wider body of work.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The contributions date from the 1980s and 1990s and the puzzles remain open, which is both a strength and a limit.
uncertainties: Much of the contribution is framework and synthesis, and the Committee may judge the discrete conceptual breakthrough to be smaller than in other candidates.
Credit overlap with other international macro contributors (e.g. Dornbusch, Krugman, Mundell-Fleming lineage).
Open puzzles may reduce the sense of settled results.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High. The China-shock papers and the task-based approach to technology changed how economists and policymakers understand labour-market adjustment to trade and automation. Both causal evidence and policy relevance are strong.
assessment.attribution: The China-shock work is clearly Autor-Dorn-Hanson. The task framework adds Autor's work with Levy, Murnane and Katz. Katz is credited on the candidate but is not proposed here, so some of the technology-side credit is left out.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature. The work is 10-20 years old, and replication and critique are extensive, including debate over magnitudes and longer-run adjustment. It is influential but the evidence is still developing.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee views the China-shock work as sufficiently established, given the continuing debate on persistence and magnitude.
Optimal trio is debatable: Katz's role in the skill-premium literature could justify his inclusion.
Combining trade and technology strands in one award may blur the prize motivation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High. Collateral constraints and the amplification of shocks through balance sheets (Kiyotaki-Moore) and the financial accelerator provide the standard macro-financial mechanism behind credit cycles. The mechanism was central to analysis of the 2008 crisis and its aftermath.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki-Moore is a tight joint contribution. Gertler is credited for the financial accelerator, shared with Bernanke, who was already honoured in 2022 for related work. Gilchrist is excluded, and Gertler also features in B036, so credit and overlap need care.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The central papers date from the 1990s, with long-standing and extensive follow-up and empirical application after 2008.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize for banking and financial crises through Bernanke.
Whether a two-person Kiyotaki-Moore award would be preferred to a three-person one.
Direct empirical identification of the mechanism is harder than for other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High on impact. Long-run top-income and wealth series built from tax data changed measurement and public debate on inequality, and created a widely used data infrastructure. The scientific merit is clearer in data construction than in the theoretical interpretation.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the central originators of the top-income series. Zucman's contribution concerns offshore wealth and distributional accounts, which are more recent. Saez also appears in B001, which supports the case for his body of work.
assessment.maturity: Mixed. The Piketty-Saez work is more than 20 years old, but the later wealth, offshore and distributional-accounts work is newer and still contested on methodology.
uncertainties: Methodological critiques of capitalisation-based wealth estimates and the treatment of transfers and taxes.
Whether the Committee gives more weight to the data contribution than to the policy-oriented framing.
Zucman's inclusion may be seen as premature relative to the earlier contributions.
